title: Kit proof
summary: The real board, the real rules and the real computer player in one small page. Every demo starts from this kit.
problem: A mockup that does not use the real art and the real rules can promise what the game cannot do.
idea: One shared kit: the painted board in DOM and CSS, the King Down engine, the app's colours and type, and a capture tool that checks each demo.

borrows.what: One set of parts that every screen uses, so the demos look like one product.

options.name: Start
options.summary: The sample army before the first move.

options.name: A piece is selected
options.summary: The Archer shows its moves and its two shots.

options.name: After two moves
options.summary: The move feed shows each move as a short sentence with the piece's icon.

options.name: The Archer shoots
options.summary: The shot flies, the Bishop falls, and the feed tells why.

recommendation: Build every demo on this kit. Link it from the demo page; do not copy or change it.
notes: Play White against the Beginner computer player. Tap or drag a piece. Long press, hover or the I key shows what a piece is.
New game gives a random army. Undo takes back your move and the computer's answer.
The engine is the app's own code (src/rules, src/ai), built into kit/kd-engine.js.
